run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:42:42Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert concerns service frontend-proxy (namespace otel-demo). Its own telemetry shows a small but real error signal: ingress spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 38.03 in the hour 22:42:42–23:42:42 versus 13011.15 UNSET ingress spans, while its egress spans recorded no error-status spans. The concrete error responses observed are 504 UT response_timeout (Envoy route timeout of 15000 ms) on GET /api/data and 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on /api/products, /api/cart, /api/data and /api/recommendations, logged 23:22:55–23:31:46. In the one 504 trace sampled, the frontend took 21.97 s for GET /api/data and its call to ad took 21.97 s (ad server span 19.70 s), and ad's flagd ResolveBoolean spans took 2.80 s and 5.49 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and a flagd span carrying otel.status_description "context deadline exceeded". A second, larger burst of frontend-proxy errors (124 and 128 error spans in the two 2-minute windows ending 23:46:42 and 23:47:42) consists of HTTP 500 responses that the frontend returned (via_upstream) for /api/cart, /api/checkout and /api/products between 23:45:39 and 23:46:41, with frontend error spans only for cart/checkout operations (CartService/AddItem, GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, tcp.connect) in the single minute 23:45:42–23:46:42, immediately after ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d replaced the single cart pod at 23:45:12–23:45:15. The flagd ConfigMap currently has cartFailure="on" ("Fail cart service") and every other fault flag off, but cart itself recorded no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the 10 minutes ending 23:52:42 and its logs show normal AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync handling at 23:46:54–23:46:58, so the on-state of cartFailure is recorded as a candidate, not as a demonstrated cause. All 21 deployments are 1/1 ready and all pods Running/Ready; only fraud-detection has a restart (OOMKilled, exit 137, at 23:50:42, after both bursts). The alert's own rule expression is not present in the target Prometheus, so which evaluation window produced the 23:42:42 firing cannot be verified. No single originating object is established by its own fault evidence, so no root cause is named.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded 38.03 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation "ingress" against 13011.15 UNSET ingress spans in the hour 22:42:42–23:42:42, and 0 error-status spans on operation "router frontend egress" (12354.92 UNSET) in the same hour.

frontend-proxy access logs between 23:22:55 and 23:31:46 show 504 "UT response_timeout" on GET /api/data (15000–15002 ms) and 503 "UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" on /api/products/{id}, /api/cart, /api/data and /api/recommendations, all with the frontend as upstream.

In trace d4af8b1eed12c220415e404f05a06a0a the frontend-proxy ingress span returned 504 after 15.0 s while the frontend served GET /api/data in 21.97 s; the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span took 21.97 s and ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span 19.70 s; ad's flagd ResolveBoolean spans took 2.80 s and 5.49 s with rpc.grpc.status_code=4 and a flagd span carried otel.status_description "context deadline exceeded" (rpc.grpc.status_code=2, 39 us).

The 503 trace c40b3222b9a63859e138ddf42bd9991a contains only four spans: load-generator user_get_recommendations, load-generator GET 503, frontend-proxy ingress 503 and frontend-proxy "router frontend egress" with http.status_code=0 and error=true; no frontend span exists in that trace, i.e. the frontend never emitted a response for it.

The 2-minute ingress error series shows a first cluster (51.7 errors in the window ending 23:24:42, declining through 4.0/2.7/2.7/1.3/2.7/2.7/4.0/2.7/2.7/2.7 per 2 minutes) reaching 0 from the window ending 23:36:42 through 23:45:42, then 124 and 128 errors in the windows ending 23:46:42 and 23:47:42, followed by 5.33, 1.33, 1.33, 1.33 and 0.

frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans exist in the range 23:40:42–23:52:42 only at the two evaluation points ending 23:46:42 and 23:47:42, with per-operation increases GET /api/cart 30.67, POST /api/cart 69.33, POST /api/checkout 24, executing api route /api/cart 100, executing api route /api/checkout 24, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 69.33, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 30.67, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 24 and tcp.connect 9.33; all were 0 at every other point in that range.

frontend-proxy access logs between 23:45:39 and 23:46:41 show the frontend itself returning HTTP 500 (via_upstream, 21-byte bodies) for POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, POST /api/checkout and GET /api/products/{id}, plus 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} at 23:46:29–23:46:30, and a return to 200 on POST /api/cart at 23:46:09 and 23:46:41.

Kubernetes events in otel-demo record Deployment cart "Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1" at 23:45:12, ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d "Created pod: cart-84889c965d-tkxdz" at 23:45:12, old pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 "Killing" and ReplicaSet cart-755465879b "Deleted pod" at 23:45:15 and cart "Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0" at 23:45:15.

ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d (owner Deployment cart) was created 2026-11-17T23:45:12Z with 1 ready replica while cart-755465879b has 0 replicas, and ReplicaSet flagd-77f6d5b95d (owner Deployment flagd) was created 2026-11-17T23:15:57Z while flagd-c47676d99 has 0 replicas; all other otel-demo ReplicaSets were created at 23:14:02–23:14:05.

The cart Deployment carries annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2, strategy RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, env FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013; the flagd Deployment is also revision 2 (image ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8, GOMEMLIMIT=60MiB) and the frontend Deployment is revision 1.

The cart container logged normal request handling after the burst, e.g. "EmptyCartAsync called with userId=...", "GetCartAsync called with userId=33cd6c24-..." and "AddItemAsync called with userId=33cd6c24-..., productId=OLJCESPC7Z, quantity=5" at 23:46:54.514–23:46:58.211.

In the 10-minute window ending 23:52:42 the only STATUS_CODE_ERROR series containing service_name=cart is cart's "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" with value 0; no cart operation (POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, AddItem, EmptyCart) appears with STATUS_CODE_ERROR, while frontend's error operations listed in the same view are the cart/checkout ones.

ConfigMap flagd-config in otel-demo has key demo.flagd.json in which flag "cartFailure" has defaultVariant "on" (state ENABLED, description "Fail cart service", variants off=false/on=true), while adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure's alternatives and the other fault flags (emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) are all defaultVariant "off".

frontend-proxy's own resources and process are not degraded: its container had 0 restarts, ~19.4 MiB working set against a 50Mi limit, a 30m CPU limit and a CFS throttled-period ratio of only 0.059–0.132 across 23:23–23:40, and its error responses are upstream responses/terminations rather than locally generated failures.
All 21 otel-demo deployments report desired=1, available=1, ready=1, and all 21 pods are phase Running with ready=true and restartCount 0 except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh (restartCount 1).

Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh has a container lastState terminated with exitCode 137 and reason OOMKilled, finishedAt 2026-11-17T23:50:42Z (startedAt 23:15:49Z); events show container fraud-detection "Created"/"Started" at 23:50:43.

ad's container has limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi; flagd's container has limits cpu 250m / memory 512Mi and requests 100m/120Mi with GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB; none of ad, cart, flagd or fraud-detection defines a readinessProbe or livenessProbe, and frontend has cpu limit 100m while frontend-proxy has cpu limit 30m.

CFS throttling (throttled periods / total periods) for the ad container was 0.633 at 23:24:12, 0.499 at 23:24:42 and 0.342 at 23:25:12, falling to 0.09–0.14 by 23:31–23:40; the frontend container stayed at 0.31–0.45 throughout 23:23–23:40, flagd's container was 0, and frontend-proxy's 0.059–0.132.

ad's CPU usage fell from 0.0388 cores at 23:24:12 to 0.011 cores at 23:36:12 while its memory working set stayed flat at ~323–337 MiB (limit 450Mi), and flagd's working set stayed flat at ~32–33.6 MiB (GOMEMLIMIT 60MiB); flagd recorded no CFS throttling.

Traffic was flat across the first error episode: ad's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds counted 86–124 spans per sample interval and frontend-proxy ingress 1194–1500 spans per sample interval between 23:24:42 and 23:38:42, so no request surge coincided with the errors.

In the hour ending 23:42:42 the services with STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were frontend-proxy 38.03, recommendation 2.06, ad 1.05, fraud-detection 1.04 and 0 for accounting, frontend and payment; frontend's own operations (GET, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data, POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, the api-route spans and its grpc client spans) all show 0 error spans in that hour.

The 503/504 frontend-proxy errors in the hour before the alert are a latency consequence, not a proxy fault: frontend requests to /api/data blocked on ad, whose flag evaluations against flagd returned DEADLINE_EXCEEDED (2.80 s and 5.49 s, rpc.grpc.status_code=4, flagd span description "context deadline exceeded"), so the frontend's 21.97 s response exceeded frontend-proxy's 15000 ms route timeout (504 UT) and some connections were terminated before a response started (503 UC).

The second, larger frontend-proxy error burst (frontend HTTP 500s on cart/checkout routes, 23:45:39–23:46:41) is a transient consequence of the cart Deployment rollout: ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d replaced the only cart pod at 23:45:12–23:45:15, the frontend's cart gRPC calls error at connection level (grpc CartService/AddItem, GetCart and tcp.connect error spans) while cart itself logged normal request handling, and the errors stopped within about one minute.

Candidate fault-injection setting: ConfigMap flagd-config's flag cartFailure is switched on ("Fail cart service") and could be injecting cart failures that surface as the frontend's 500s on /api/cart, /api/checkout and the product routes.

The cartFailure candidate is weakened by cart's own evidence: cart recorded no error-status spans in the 10 minutes ending 23:52:42, its logs contain normal AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync handling at 23:46:54–23:46:58, and frontend-proxy logged successful POST /api/cart 200 responses at 23:46:09 and 23:46:41 while cartFailure is still "on" in the ConfigMap, so the observed failures are not shown to be cart-application failures.

frontend-proxy does not appear to be failing because of its own resource exhaustion or restart: the pod has 0 restarts, ~19.4 MiB working set against a 50Mi limit, a 0.059–0.132 throttled-period ratio and no previous container instance, and the slow/error responses it produced carry the frontend as upstream.

Obtain the RequestErrorRate rule expression and the Alertmanager evaluation history for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy so the "current: 0.01111111111111111" value and the 23:42:42 start can be tied to a specific window, since the target Prometheus exposed no alerting rules to verify it.

Review change history/audit records for Deployment cart (revision 2, new ReplicaSet at 23:45:12), Deployment flagd (revision 2, new ReplicaSet at 23:15:57) and the demo.flagd.json data of ConfigMap flagd-config, because the change history integration is absent and object state alone cannot show what changed these workloads.

Compare ad's 50m CPU limit with its CFS throttling (0.63 of periods at 23:24:12) and, if the flag-evaluation latency recurs, consider raising the ad CPU limit or increasing flagd client deadlines, because ad sat at its limit during the episode while request traffic stayed flat.

Have a human check fraud-detection's memory limit (400Mi) against its OOMKill (exit 137 at 23:50:42) and capture frontend/flagd container logs from another source, since the log pipeline returned no lines for those containers in this run.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not present in the target Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned no alerting rules (a no_data view), so the rule expression, its window and the meaning of "current: 0.01111111111111111" are unknown and the 23:42:42 firing cannot be tied to one evaluation window; the query result cannot be cited as evidence of absence.

The change_history integration is not available, so what changed the cart Deployment template (revision 2, 23:45:12) and the flagd Deployment template (revision 2, 23:15:57), and whether or when the demo.flagd.json values (including cartFailure="on") were changed, is unknown; ConfigMaps and workloads were read only in their state at query time.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 23:18–23:42 (0 bytes read) and the flagd containers produced no readable lines for 23:14–23:30, so the frontend's and flagd's own error text and the frontend's reason for terminating connections or returning 500 are unknown.

A filtered query for error/exception/failure lines in the cart container's logs 23:44–23:52 returned no matching lines (no_data over 3382 lines read), so cart-side error text is unobserved rather than proven absent.

Jaeger returned no frontend traces after roughly 23:31, so the 23:45:39–23:46:41 HTTP 500 burst has no trace-level error messages, and the sampled 503 traces show no frontend span at all — the frontend's participation in those traces remains unknown.

The returned Prometheus series end around 23:52 in this run; the state of frontend-proxy's error signal between 23:52 and the alert capture time (00:03:56) is unknown, so whether the alert is still firing on the later burst cannot be established.

The value of the cartFailure flag and of all other flagd flags during 23:22–23:47 is unknown; only the ConfigMap's state at query time was read, and the flagd-ui/flagd not exposing evaluation history was not checked.
A networkpolicy query for otel-demo returned no objects (no_data), so whether a policy blocked ad→flagd or frontend→cart traffic is unknown.

Whether ad's 2.80 s / 5.49 s flag-evaluation stalls were caused by ad-side pauses (GC/thread starvation) or by flagd-side slowness cannot be determined: ad's logs had no matching lines, no JVM metrics were found, and flagd's own span completed in 39 us.

The exact number of unique requests behind the frontend-proxy error ratio is unknown; trace span counts and the ingress span count are not unique request counts, so the alert's denominator could not be reproduced.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition and Alertmanager notification history for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy to fix the evaluation window that produced the 23:42:42 start and the 0.0111 value.
Pull Kubernetes audit/change history for Deployment cart (rev 2), Deployment flagd (rev 2) and ConfigMap flagd-config, including when cartFailure was set to "on".
Re-query frontend and flagd container logs from a complete log backend for 23:20–23:50, since the pod log API returned no lines for those containers.
Check whether flagd's flag-evaluation latency (ad's ResolveBoolean spans of 2.8–5.5 s with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED) recurs, and correlate it with ad CPU throttling at its 50m limit.
Confirm whether the fraud-detection OOMKill at 23:50:42 and its 400Mi memory limit have any relationship to checkout failures, since the OOM occurred after the observed 500 burst.
